nodes.name: Nilpotent orbit $\mathcal{O}$
nodes.statement:
For each root type $\star$ we work with a nilpotent orbit $\mathcal{O}$ in
the Lie algebra of a classical group.

nodes.name: BV dual
nodes.statement_short: The BV dual of the orbit is a partition with per-type parity conditions (table).

nodes.name: Column and row lengths $\mathbf{c}_i$, $\mathbf{r}_i$
nodes.statement:
From $\check{\mathcal{O}}$ we read off column lengths
$\mathbf{c}_1 \geq \mathbf{c}_2 \geq \cdots$ and row lengths
$\mathbf{r}_1 \geq \mathbf{r}_2 \geq \cdots$.

nodes.name: DRC symbols
nodes.statement: The five \emph{DRC symbols} are \[ \{\bullet,\ s,\ r,\ c,\ d\}. \] Symbols other than $\bullet$ are called \emph{non-dot}.
nodes.label: def:drc_symbols

nodes.name: Layer order
nodes.statement: The \emph{layer order} is a function $\mathrm{layerOrd} : \mathrm{DRCSymbol} \to \mathbb{N}$ given by \[ \mathrm{layerOrd}(\bullet) = 0,\ \mathrm{layerOrd}(s) = 1,\ \mathrm{layerOrd}(r) = 2,\ \mathrm{layerOrd}(c) = 3,\ \mathrm{layerOrd}(d) = 4. \] This is the linear order $\bullet < s < r < c < d$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear order on DRC symbols: dot < s < r < c < d, encoded as layerOrd values 0..4.
nodes.label: def:layerOrd

nodes.name: Tail contribution
nodes.statement: Paper Eq.~(11.5). Each DRC symbol contributes a pair of non-negative integers to the tail signature: \[ \mathrm{tailContrib}(\bullet) = (1,1),\ \mathrm{tailContrib}(s) = (0, 2),\ \mathrm{tailContrib}(r) = (2, 0), \] \[ \mathrm{tailContrib}(c) = (1, 1),\ \mathrm{tailContrib}(d) = (1, 1). \] In particular the two components always sum to~$2$.
nodes.statement_short: Each DRC symbol contributes a pair of nonnegative integers summing to 2 to the tail signature (Eq. 11.5).
nodes.label: def:tailContrib

nodes.name: Young diagram
nodes.statement: A Young diagram $\mu$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb{N}^2$ which is a \emph{down-set} under $(i, j) \leq (i', j') \iff i \leq i' \land j \leq j'$. Columns $j$ have lengths $\mu.\mathrm{colLen}(j) = |\{i : (i, j) \in \mu\}|$.
nodes.label: def:yd

nodes.name: Painted Young diagram
nodes.statement: A \emph{painted Young diagram} is a triple $D = (\mu, \mathcal{P}, \mathrm{layerMono})$ where: \begin{enumerate} \item $\mu$ is a Young diagram (the \emph{shape}). \item $\mathcal{P} : \mathbb{N}^2 \to \mathrm{DRCSymbol}$ is a paint function with $\mathcal{P}(i, j) = \bullet$ for $(i, j) \notin \mu$ (paint outside the shape is $\bullet$). \item \textbf{layer monotonicity}: for all $(i_1, j_1), (i_2, j_2)$ with $i_1 \leq i_2$ and $j_1 \leq j_2$, if $(i_2, j_2) \in \mu$ then $\mathrm{layerOrd}(\mathcal{P}(i_1, j_1)) \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(\mathcal{P}(i_2, j_2))$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A Young diagram with a paint function into DRC symbols, dot outside the shape, satisfying layer monotonicity.
nodes.label: def:pyd

nodes.name: $\mathrm{dotScolLen}$ — dot-and-s column length
nodes.statement: For a painted Young diagram $D$, $\mathrm{dotScolLen}(D, j)$ is the number of cells in column $j$ whose paint is $\bullet$ or $s$ (equivalently, the largest $k$ such that every cell $(i, j)$ with $i < k$ has $\mathrm{layerOrd}(\mathcal{P}(i, j)) \leq 1$).
nodes.statement_short: Number of cells in column j painted dot or s.
nodes.label: def:dotScolLen

nodes.name: Root type
nodes.statement: A \emph{root type} $\gamma \in \{B^+,\ B^-,\ C,\ D,\ M\}$ selects a set of allowed paint symbols for $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ (see below).
nodes.label: def:RootType

nodes.name: Symbol allowances per root type
nodes.statement: The following table gives the allowed DRC symbols for $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ (paper Def.~2.25): \[ \begin{array}{l|ll} \gamma & \mathcal{P}\text{ allowed} & \mathcal{Q}\text{ allowed} \\\hline B^+ / B^- & \{\bullet, c\} & \{\bullet, s, r, d\} \\ C & \{\bullet, r, c, d\} & \{\bullet, s\} \\ D & \{\bullet, s, r, c, d\} & \{\bullet\} \\ M = \tilde{C} & \{\bullet, s, c\} & \{\bullet, r, d\} \\ \end{array} \] The $B^+/B^-$ distinction corresponds to a tag on the extended DRC diagram.
nodes.statement_short: Table of allowed DRC symbols for P and Q per root type (paper Def. 2.25).
nodes.label: def:sym_allowed

nodes.name: Painted Bipartition
nodes.statement: A \emph{painted bipartition} (PBP) is $\tau = (\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}, \gamma)$ where $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ are painted Young diagrams with root type $\gamma$ satisfying: \begin{enumerate} \item \textbf{sym\_P, sym\_Q}: $\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{paint}(i, j)$ is in the allowed set for $\mathcal{P}$ determined by $\gamma$ (Def.~\ref{def:sym_allowed}), and likewise for $\mathcal{Q}$. \item \textbf{dot\_match}: $\mathcal{P}(i,j) = \bullet \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{Q}(i,j) = \bullet$ (the outside-shape convention makes this an equivalence between cell memberships). \item \textbf{row\_s, row\_r}: each row contains at most one $s$ across $\mathcal{P} \cup \mathcal{Q}$; similarly at most one $r$. \item \textbf{col\_c\_P / col\_c\_Q}: each column of $\mathcal{P}$ has at most one $c$; same for $\mathcal{Q}$. \item \textbf{col\_d\_P / col\_d\_Q}: each column has at most one $d$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A PBP is a pair of painted Young diagrams with root type, obeying symbol allowances, dot matching and row/column uniqueness of s, r, c, d.
nodes.genus: painted Young diagrams with root type $\gamma$
nodes.label: def:PBP

nodes.name: Notation $\iota_\wp$, $\jmath_\wp$
nodes.statement: The notation $\iota_\wp := \mathcal{P}$ and $\jmath_\wp := \mathcal{Q}$ appears in the paper and is used interchangeably. The index $\wp$ is a \emph{primitive pair set} which we usually omit, assuming the canonical $\wp$.

nodes.name: PBPSet — PBPs of fixed shape
nodes.statement: For $\gamma$ a root type and $\mu_P, \mu_Q$ Young diagrams, \[ \PBP_\gamma(\mu_P, \mu_Q) := \{\tau \in \mathrm{PBP} \mid \tau.\gamma = \gamma,\ \tau.\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{shape} = \mu_P,\ \tau.\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{shape} = \mu_Q\}. \] Given a dual partition $dp$, we set $\PBP_\gamma(\check{\mathcal{O}}) := \PBP_\gamma(\mu_P(dp), \mu_Q(dp))$ where $\mu_P, \mu_Q$ are derived from $dp$.
nodes.statement_short: Set of PBPs of root type gamma with prescribed shapes; also indexed by a dual partition.
nodes.label: def:PBPSet

nodes.name: PBP signature $\Sign(\tau)$
nodes.statement: The signature $\Sign(\tau) = (p_\tau, q_\tau) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ counts paint symbols weighted by paint multiplicities (paper Eq.~(3.3)). Specifically, denoting by $\#_\sigma$ the count of symbol $\sigma$ in $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, and by $n_s, n_r$ the total $s, r$ counts across both, \[ p_\tau = n_r, \qquad q_\tau = n_s, \] with appropriate bookkeeping for $\bullet, c, d$ counts and per-$\gamma$ variations. For D type: $p_\tau = \#_{\bullet,\iota} + \#_{\bullet,\jmath} + 2\#_{r,\iota} + \#_{c,\iota} + \#_{d,\iota}$ (and similarly for $q_\tau$ with $s$ in place of $r$).
nodes.statement_short: Signature (p,q) of a PBP counting paint symbols with multiplicities (paper Eq. 3.3).
nodes.label: def:signature_pbp

nodes.name: Epsilon $\eps_\tau$
nodes.statement: (Paper Eq.~(3.6).) $\eps_\tau \in \{0, 1\}$ is $1$ iff column~0 of $\mathcal{P}$ (or $\mathcal{Q}$, per $\gamma$) contains a $d$.
nodes.statement_short: epsilon_tau is 1 iff column 0 of P (or Q) contains a d (paper Eq. 3.6).
nodes.label: def:epsilon_pbp

nodes.name: Total cell count $|\tau|$
nodes.statement: $|\tau| := |\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{shape}.\mathrm{cells}| + |\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{shape}.\mathrm{cells}|$.
nodes.label: def:cardCells

nodes.name: Dual partition legality
nodes.statement: A \emph{dual partition} $dp$ is a \texttt{List ℕ} that is sorted $\geq$ (strictly decreasing with possible ties). Validity conditions: \begin{itemize} \item B-type / M-type: every entry is even and positive. \item D-type / C-type: every entry is odd. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: def:DualPart

nodes.name: Column lengths from dp
nodes.statement: For each root type, functions compute the column-length lists of $\mu_P$ and $\mu_Q$ from $dp$. For example (D type): $\mu_P(dp)$ has column lengths $(dp_1 + 1)/2, (dp_2 + 1)/2, \ldots$, etc.
nodes.statement_short: Column-length lists of mu_P and mu_Q computed from a dual partition, per root type.
nodes.label: def:dpartColLens

nodes.name: paint translation $\mathrm{translateM}$
nodes.statement: The involution \[ \mathrm{translateM}(\bullet) = \bullet,\quad \mathrm{translateM}(s) = r,\quad \mathrm{translateM}(r) = s,\quad \mathrm{translateM}(c) = d,\quad \mathrm{translateM}(d) = c. \] Note that $\mathrm{translateM}$ preserves $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ modulo the swaps.
nodes.statement_short: Involution on DRC symbols swapping s<->r and c<->d.
nodes.label: def:translateM

nodes.name: shape shift M
nodes.statement: Let $\tau = (\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}, M) \in \PBP_M(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$. Given shapes $(\mu_P', \mu_Q')$ whose column~0 is swapped with $(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$ (i.e., $(i, 0) \in \mu_P' \iff (i, 0) \in \mu_Q$; columns $\geq 1$ unchanged), define $\mathrm{shapeShiftM}(\tau) \in \PBP_M(\mu_P', \mu_Q')$ by \begin{align*} \tau'.\mathcal{P}(i, 0) &= \mathrm{translateM}(\tau.\mathcal{Q}(i, 0)), & \tau'.\mathcal{P}(i, j+1) &= \tau.\mathcal{P}(i, j+1), \\ \tau'.\mathcal{Q}(i, 0) &= \mathrm{translateM}(\tau.\mathcal{P}(i, 0)), & \tau'.\mathcal{Q}(i, j+1) &= \tau.\mathcal{Q}(i, j+1). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: M-type shape shift: swap column 0 between P and Q applying translateM, keeping other columns.
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftM

nodes.name: shape shift M is an involution
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{shapeShiftM} \circ \mathrm{shapeShiftM} = \mathrm{id}$.
nodes.statement_short: shapeShiftM is an involution.
nodes.label: lem:shapeShiftM_involution

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{translateM}$ is an involution on DRC symbols; applying it twice gives identity. The column-0 swap is also self-inverse. Hence so is their composition.
nodes.statement_short: translateM and the column-0 swap are both involutions, hence so is the composite.

nodes.name: Lemma 10.3 M — PBPSet cardinality equality
nodes.statement: $|\PBP_M(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_M(\mu_P', \mu_Q')|$ for any column-0 swapped shape pair.
nodes.statement_short: M-type PBP sets of column-0 swapped shape pairs have equal size.
assumptions: for any column-0 swapped shape pair
nodes.label: lem:10_3_M

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{shapeShiftM}$ is a bijection (its own inverse). The PBP axioms (sym, dot\_match, monotonicity, row/column constraints) are preserved under the translation (see [BMSZb] Sec.~10.2; also the axiom-by-axiom verification in the Lean proof).
nodes.statement_short: shapeShiftM is its own inverse hence a bijection, and preserves the PBP axioms.

nodes.name: Prop 10.2 M — PBP count independent of $\wp$
nodes.statement: The cardinality equality extends to arbitrary column-0 swap sequences.
nodes.statement_short: M-type PBP count is invariant under arbitrary sequences of column-0 swaps.
nodes.label: prop:10_2_M

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Iterated application of the column-0 swap Lemma~\ref{lem:10_3_M} transports $\tau$ through any sequence of primitive-pair-set configurations.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the column-0 swap lemma.

nodes.name: Shape shift C setup: $\tau$
nodes.statement: Let $\tau \in \PBP_C(\check{\mathcal{O}}, \wp)$ with $(1, 2) \in \mathrm{PP}_\star(\check{\mathcal{O}})$ and $(1, 2) \notin \wp$.

nodes.name: Shape shift C setup: $k$, $k_\uparrow$, $\wp_\uparrow$
nodes.statement:
Set
\[ k := \mathbf{c}_1(\iota_\wp),\qquad k_\uparrow := \mathbf{c}_1(\iota_{\wp_\uparrow}), \]
where $\wp_\uparrow := \wp \cup \{(1, 2)\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a C-type PBP with (1,2) a primitive pair not in wp; set k, k_up as first column lengths for wp and wp_up.

nodes.name: $k_\uparrow > k \geq 1$
nodes.statement: By the PP assumption, $k_\uparrow > k \geq 1$.

nodes.name: $\tau_\uparrow.\mathcal{Q}$
nodes.statement: Since $\jmath$ is unchanged, $\tau_\uparrow.\mathcal{Q}(i, j) := \tau.\mathcal{Q}(i, j)$ for all $(i, j)$.

nodes.name: shape shift C — main dispatcher
nodes.statement: The paint function $\mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}$ dispatches to one of the four sub-case formulas (Def.~\ref{def:shapeShiftC_case_a1}, \ref{def:shapeShiftC_case_a2}, \ref{def:shapeShiftC_case_b1}, \ref{def:shapeShiftC_case_b2}) according to $\mathcal{P}_\tau(k, 1)$ and $\mathcal{P}_\tau(k - 1, 1)$, where $k := \mathbf{c}_1(\iota_\wp)$ and $k_\uparrow := \mathbf{c}_1(\iota_{\wp_\uparrow})$. Set $\alpha_0 := \mathcal{P}_\tau(k, 1)$ when non-$\bullet$.
nodes.section: 3.2.2 Case analysis for the new paint
nodes.statement_short: C-type shape shift paint dispatches to four sub-cases according to P_tau(k,1) and P_tau(k-1,1).
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftC_paint

nodes.name: sub-case (a.1): previous-cell is c
nodes.statement: Applies when $\alpha_0 \neq \bullet$, $k \geq 2$, and $\mathcal{P}_\tau(k - 1, 1) = c$. The new paint is \[ \mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}(i, j) = \begin{cases} r & j = 1,\ k - 1 \leq i \leq k_\uparrow - 2 \\ c & (i, j) = (k_\uparrow - 1, 1) \\ d & (i, j) = (k_\uparrow, 1) \\ \mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
nodes.section: 3.2.2 Case analysis for the new paint
nodes.statement_short: New paint when top is non-dot, k>=2 and previous cell is c: r run, then c, then d.
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftC_case_a1

nodes.name: sub-case (a.2): default for non-dot top
nodes.statement: Applies when $\alpha_0 \neq \bullet$ and the (a.1) condition on $\mathcal{P}_\tau(k - 1, 1)$ fails. The new paint is \[ \mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}(i, j) = \begin{cases} r & j = 1,\ k \leq i \leq k_\uparrow - 1 \\ \alpha_0 & (i, j) = (k_\uparrow, 1) \\ \mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
nodes.section: 3.2.2 Case analysis for the new paint
nodes.statement_short: New paint when top is non-dot and (a.1) fails: r run then alpha_0 at row k_up.
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftC_case_a2

nodes.name: sub-case (b.1): Q col-2 lift (deferred)
nodes.statement: Applies when $\alpha_0 = \bullet$, $\mathbf{c}_2(\iota_\wp) = k$, and $\mathcal{P}_\tau(k, 2) = r$. The new paint formula modifies column~1 of $\jmath$-reachable cells: \[ \mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}(i, j) = \begin{cases} r & j = 1,\ k \leq i \leq k_\uparrow - 1 \\ c & (i, j) = (\mathbf{c}_2(\iota_\wp), 2) \\ d & (i, j) = (k_\uparrow, 1) \\ \mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \] The Lean formalization uses a fallback constructor (\texttt{shiftPaintP\_C\_concrete\_case\_b1\_fallback}); a full constructive case (b.1) handler is deferred future work.
nodes.section: 3.2.2 Case analysis for the new paint
nodes.statement_short: New paint when top is dot, c_2=k and P(k,2)=r; Lean uses a fallback constructor.
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftC_case_b1

nodes.name: sub-case (b.2): default for dot top
nodes.statement: Applies when $\alpha_0 = \bullet$ and the (b.1) condition fails. The new paint is \[ \mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}(i, j) = \begin{cases} r & j = 1,\ k \leq i \leq k_\uparrow - 2 \\ c & (i, j) = (k - 1, 1) \\ d & (i, j) = (k_\uparrow, 1) \\ \mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j) & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
nodes.section: 3.2.2 Case analysis for the new paint
nodes.statement_short: New paint when top is dot and (b.1) fails: r run, c at k-1, d at k_up.
nodes.label: def:shapeShiftC_case_b2

nodes.name: Shape shift C produces a valid PBP
nodes.statement: The painted diagram produced by any of the four sub-cases of Def.~\ref{def:shapeShiftC_paint} satisfies all PBP axioms: the allowed symbol sets (\texttt{sym\_P}, \texttt{sym\_Q}), layer monotonicity, the \texttt{dot\_match} invariant, and the row / column uniqueness conditions (\texttt{row\_s}, \texttt{row\_r}, \texttt{col\_c\_P}, \texttt{col\_c\_Q}, \texttt{col\_d\_P}, \texttt{col\_d\_Q}).
nodes.statement_short: Every C-type shape-shift sub-case yields a painted diagram satisfying all PBP axioms.
assumptions: The painted diagram produced by any of the four sub-cases of Def.~\ref{def:shapeShiftC_paint}
nodes.label: cor:shapeShiftC_valid

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We check each axiom case-by-case. \textbf{sym\_P}: The new paint function outputs values only in $\{r, c, d\}$ (the forced values in the modified region of column~1) or $\mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j)$ (unchanged cells, inheriting validity from $\tau$). Both lie in the C-type $\mathcal{P}$-allowed set $\{\bullet, s, r, c, d\}$. Formalized as \texttt{shiftPaintP\_C\_concrete\_case\_a1\_allowed} and the analogous \texttt{a2}, \texttt{b2} variants. \textbf{sym\_Q}: $\mathcal{Q}$ is unchanged, so the axiom carries over directly from $\tau$. \textbf{layer monotonicity}: In case (a.1) the sequence $\cdots r\ c\ d$ has monotone $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ ($2 \le 3 \le 4$); the pattern is preserved across sub-cases by construction of $\mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}$. \textbf{col\_c\_P, col\_d\_P}: Case (a.1) moves the pre-existing $c$ at row $k-1$ to the new position $k_\uparrow - 1$ (rewriting the old cell as $r$), hence column~1 still has exactly one $c$. The newly-introduced $d$ sits at row $k_\uparrow$; uniqueness holds because the original tail contained no $d$ at the top (by layer monotonicity on $\tau$). Formalized as \texttt{shiftPaintP\_C\_concrete\_case\_a2\_col\_c} and \texttt{shiftPaintP\_C\_concrete\_case\_a2\_col\_d}. \textbf{row\_s, row\_r}: Same-row uniqueness carries over from $\tau$ since the C-type $\mathcal{Q}$ only contains $\{\bullet, s\}$, so the modifications to $\mathcal{P}$'s column~1 cannot conflict row-wise with anything in $\mathcal{Q}$. \textbf{dot\_match}: The dot positions of $\mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow}$ agree with those of $\mathcal{Q}_{\tau_\uparrow} = \mathcal{Q}_\tau$ because the modifications only fill non-dot cells in the strictly extended tail region $[k, k_\uparrow]$. The Lean \texttt{shapeShiftC} definition exhibits all of the above by constructing the final PBP with every axiom verified.
nodes.statement_short: Axiom-by-axiom case check of the four sub-cases; only column 1 of P changes, Q is unchanged.

nodes.name: shape shift C identity instance
nodes.statement: The identity instance (parameterised by the trivial col-0 paint) returns the original PBP. Used as a degenerate witness.
nodes.statement_short: The identity instance of shapeShiftC returns the original PBP.
nodes.label: lem:shapeShiftC_id

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The identity instance takes $\mathcal{P}_{\tau_\uparrow} = \mathcal{P}_\tau$ pointwise, so $\tau_\uparrow = \tau$ by \texttt{PaintedYoungDiagram.ext'}.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise equality of paints and extensionality.

nodes.name: Lemma 10.3 C — PBPSet cardinality
nodes.statement: For shapes $(\mu_P', \mu_Q')$ reachable via C-type shape shift from $(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$: \[ |\PBP_C(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_C(\mu_P', \mu_Q')|. \]
nodes.statement_short: C-type PBP sets of shapes related by a C-type shape shift have equal size.
assumptions: For shapes $(\mu_P', \mu_Q')$ reachable via C-type shape shift from $(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$
nodes.label: lem:10_3_C

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The shape-shift is a bijection $(\wp, \tau) \leftrightarrow (\wp \cup \{(1,2)\}, \tau_\uparrow)$ via the case analysis in Def.~\ref{def:shapeShiftC_paint}. In particular $\mathrm{shapeShiftC\_id}$ is its own inverse (Lemma~\ref{lem:shapeShiftC_id}).
nodes.statement_short: The shape shift is a bijection via the case analysis.

nodes.name: Prop 10.2 C — PBP count independent of $\wp$
nodes.statement: Prop 10.2 C — PBP count independent of $\wp$
nodes.statement_short: C-type PBP count is independent of wp (statement left empty in the blueprint).

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By iterating Lemma~\ref{lem:10_3_C} (or its identity instance) on $\wp$-modifications.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the C-type shape-shift lemma over wp-modifications.

nodes.name: Prop 10.2 B / D — trivial
nodes.statement: $|\PBP_\gamma(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_\gamma(\mu_P, \mu_Q)|$ for $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-, D\}$. (Reflexive statement; the genuine content for B/D is the internal paint-permutation bijection, not captured at the Lean level.)
nodes.statement_short: For B and D types the wp-independence statement is reflexive in the formalization.
nodes.label: prop:10_2_BD

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For B/D in our formalization $\PBP_\gamma$ is already the $\wp = \emptyset$ instance. The paper's shape-preserving paint-permutation bijection is not reflected at the Lean level and the statement degenerates to reflexivity.
nodes.statement_short: PBP_gamma is already the wp=empty instance, so the statement is reflexivity.

nodes.name: Descent maps
nodes.statement:
Descent maps remove the left-most column of $\mathcal{P}$, of $\mathcal{Q}$, or
of both, producing a PBP on a shifted shape.

nodes.name: D $\to$ C paints
nodes.statement: Let $c_L(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{P}, j + 1)$ and $c_R(j) := \tau.\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(j)$. \begin{align*} (\nabla_{DC}\tau).\mathcal{P}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_L(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{P}(i, j + 1) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \\ (\nabla_{DC}\tau).\mathcal{Q}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_L(j) \\ s & c_L(j) \leq i < c_R(j) \\ \bullet & i \geq c_R(j) \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: D to C naive descent: shift P left by one column, refill with dots, and paint Q with dots and s.
nodes.label: def:descentPaint_DC

nodes.name: C $\to$ D paints
nodes.statement: $c_L(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{P}, j)$, $c_R(j) := \tau.\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(j + 1)$. \[ (\nabla_{CD}\tau).\mathcal{P}(i, j) = \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_R(j) \\ s & c_R(j) \leq i < c_L(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{P}(i, j) & i \geq c_L(j) \end{cases} \] $(\nabla_{CD}\tau).\mathcal{Q}$ is all $\bullet$ (D type has $\mathcal{Q}$-allowed $= \{\bullet\}$).
nodes.statement_short: C to D naive descent: refill P with dots and s below thresholds; Q all dots.
nodes.label: def:descentPaint_CD

nodes.name: B $\to$ M paints
nodes.statement: $c_L(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{P}, j)$, $c_R(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{Q}, j + 1)$. \begin{align*} (\nabla_{BM}\tau).\mathcal{P}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_R(j) \\ s & c_R(j) \leq i < c_L(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{P}(i, j) & i \geq c_L(j) \end{cases} \\ (\nabla_{BM}\tau).\mathcal{Q}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_R(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{Q}(i, j + 1) & i \geq c_R(j) \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: B to M naive descent: cut column 0 of Q and refill P with dots and s.
nodes.label: def:descentPaint_BM

nodes.name: M $\to$ B paints
nodes.statement: $c_L(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{P}, j + 1)$, $c_R(j) := \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau.\mathcal{Q}, j)$. \begin{align*} (\nabla_{MB}\tau).\mathcal{P}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_L(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{P}(i, j+1) & i \geq c_L(j) \end{cases} \\ (\nabla_{MB}\tau).\mathcal{Q}(i, j) &= \begin{cases} \bullet & i < c_L(j) \\ s & c_L(j) \leq i < c_R(j) \\ \tau.\mathcal{Q}(i, j) & i \geq c_R(j) \end{cases} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: M to B naive descent: cut column 0 of P and refill Q with dots and s.
nodes.label: def:descentPaint_MB

nodes.name: Double descent D type
nodes.statement_short: D-type double descent: composite of D->C and C->D descents, explicit formula.
nodes.label: def:doubleDescent_D

nodes.name: Double descent B type
nodes.statement_short: B-type double descent: composite of B->M and M->B descents, explicit formula.
nodes.label: def:doubleDescent_B

nodes.name: Lemma 10.4 C — C$\to$D descent is injective
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_P, \mu_Q$ be shapes with $\mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_Q) \leq \mu_P$. The map $\nabla_{CD} : \PBP_C(\mu_P, \mu_Q) \to \PBP_D(\mu_P, \mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_Q))$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: The C->D descent map on C-type PBPs of fixed shape is injective.
nodes.label: lem:10_4_C

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The C$\to$D descent writes $\mathcal{P}_\tau(i, j + 1)$ pointwise into $\mathcal{P}_{\nabla\tau}(i, j)$ for $i \geq c_L(j)$, and fills the dot/$s$ region uniquely. Given two C-type PBPs with equal descent, we recover $\mathcal{P}_\tau$ cell-by-cell.
nodes.statement_short: Recover P_tau cell-by-cell from the descent.

nodes.name: Lemma 10.4 B — B$\to$M + signature is injective
nodes.statement: For $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-\}$ and $\tau_1, \tau_2 \in \PBP_\gamma(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$ with the interlacing shape hypothesis $\mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau_i.\mathcal{P}, j) \geq \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau_i.\mathcal{Q}, j + 1)$: if $\nabla_{BM}\tau_1 = \nabla_{BM}\tau_2$, $\Sign(\tau_1) = \Sign(\tau_2)$, $\eps_{\tau_1} = \eps_{\tau_2}$, then $\tau_1 = \tau_2$.
nodes.statement_short: B-type PBPs are determined by their B->M descent, signature and epsilon under interlacing.
assumptions: the interlacing shape hypothesis $\mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau_i.\mathcal{P}, j) \geq \mathrm{dotScolLen}(\tau_i.\mathcal{Q}, j + 1)$
nodes.label: lem:10_4_B

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By \texttt{PBP.descent\_inj\_B}: equal B$\to$M descents plus equal signatures plus equal $\eps$ determine the paint cell-by-cell; the interlacing hypothesis localizes the recovery.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Lean lemma PBP.descent_inj_B: descent plus signature plus epsilon determine the paint cell-by-cell.

nodes.name: Lemma 10.5 M — M$\to$B descent is injective
nodes.statement: Equal M$\to$B descent paints $\Rightarrow$ equal M-type PBPs (same shapes).
nodes.statement_short: M-type PBPs of the same shapes are determined by their M->B descent.
nodes.label: lem:10_5_M

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The M$\to$B descent is a bijection onto its image (given fixed shapes). Equal images force equal pre-images.
nodes.statement_short: The M->B descent is a bijection onto its image for fixed shapes.

nodes.name: Lemma 10.5 D — double descent + signature injective
nodes.statement: On $\PBP_D(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$, the map $\tau \mapsto (\nabla^2\tau, \Sign(\tau), \eps_\tau)$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: On D-type PBP sets, tau -> (double descent, signature, epsilon) is injective.
nodes.label: lem:10_5_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \texttt{doubleDescent\_D\_injective\_on\_PBPSet}: two D-type PBPs with equal $\nabla^2\tau$ have column-$\geq 2$ data identical; column~1 is determined by $\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}$; column~0 is determined by $(\Sign(\tau), \eps_\tau)$.
nodes.statement_short: Columns >=2 come from the double descent, column 1 from Q's column lengths, column 0 from (Sign, eps).

nodes.name: Prop 10.8(a) C primitive
nodes.statement: If $\mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \geq \mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$ (\emph{primitive case}), then \[ |\PBP_C(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_D(\mu_P, \mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_Q))|. \]
nodes.statement_short: In the primitive case, C-type PBP count equals the D-type count on the shifted shape.
nodes.label: prop:10_8_C_prim

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Under $\mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \geq \mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$, every D-type on $(\mu_P, \mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_Q))$ is in the image of the C$\to$D descent; injectivity from Lemma~\ref{lem:10_4_C}.
nodes.statement_short: Surjectivity of the C->D descent in the primitive case plus injectivity.

nodes.name: Prop 10.8(b) C balanced
nodes.statement: If $\mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0) = \mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) + 1$ (\emph{balanced case}), the C$\to$D descent image is $\{\sigma \in \PBP_D \mid \mathrm{tailClass}(\sigma) \in \{\mathrm{DD}, \mathrm{RC}\}\}$: \[ |\PBP_C(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = \#\{\mathrm{DD}\} + \#\{\mathrm{RC}\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: In the balanced case, C-type count equals the number of D-type PBPs with tail class DD or RC.
nodes.label: prop:10_8_C_bal

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The image of the C$\to$D descent in the balanced case consists exactly of the D-type PBPs with tail class $\mathrm{DD}$ or $\mathrm{RC}$: a $\mathrm{DD}$ tail corresponds to lifted $c$ in $\mathcal{P}$ col~0, $\mathrm{RC}$ to lifted $r$. Summing cardinalities gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the descent image with DD and RC tail classes and sum cardinalities.

nodes.name: Prop 10.8(a) M primitive
nodes.statement: If $\mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0) > \mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$ (\emph{primitive}): \[ |\PBP_M(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_{B^+}(\mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_P), \mu_Q)| + |\PBP_{B^-}(\mathrm{shiftLeft}(\mu_P), \mu_Q)|. \]
nodes.statement_short: In the primitive case, M-type count equals the sum of B+ and B- counts on the shifted shape.
nodes.label: prop:10_8_M_prim

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Descending M$\to$B at a primitive step splits into $B^+$ and $B^-$ branches according to the bottom-$\mathcal{Q}$ paint. Injectivity of each branch combined with the disjoint branches gives the sum.
nodes.statement_short: The M->B descent splits into disjoint injective B+ and B- branches; sum.

nodes.name: Prop 10.8(b) M balanced
nodes.statement: If $\mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0) = \mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) > 0$: \[ |\PBP_M(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = |\PBP_{B^+}(\cdots)| + |\{\sigma \in \PBP_{B^-}(\cdots) : \mathrm{layerOrd}(\sigma.\mathcal{Q}(c_2 - 1, 0)) > 1\}|. \]
nodes.statement_short: In the balanced case, M-type count is B+ count plus a restricted B- count.
nodes.label: prop:10_8_M_bal

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The balanced case image restricts $B^-$ to those with $\mathrm{layerOrd}(\sigma.\mathcal{Q}(c_2 - 1, 0)) > 1$ (otherwise the descent produces a layer conflict); $B^+$ is unrestricted. Summing gives the card.
nodes.statement_short: Characterise the balanced-case image (B- restricted by layer order) and sum.

nodes.name: Prop 10.9 D — double descent is injective modulo $(\Sign, \eps)$
nodes.statement: For D-type PBPs $\tau_1, \tau_2$ with identical shapes, identical $\nabla^2\tau$, identical $\Sign$, and identical $\eps$: $\tau_1 = \tau_2$.
nodes.statement_short: D-type PBPs with equal shapes, double descent, signature and epsilon coincide.
assumptions: For D-type PBPs $\tau_1, \tau_2$ with identical shapes, identical $\nabla^2\tau$, identical $\Sign$, and identical $\eps$
nodes.label: prop:10_9_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:10_5_D}: equal $(\nabla^2\tau, \Sign(\tau), \eps_\tau)$ determines $\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the D-type double-descent injectivity lemma.

nodes.name: Prop 10.9 B — double descent injective
nodes.statement: Analogue for $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-\}$, under the interlacing constraint.
nodes.statement_short: B-type analogue of double-descent injectivity under interlacing.
nodes.label: prop:10_9_B

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Immediate from Lemma~\ref{lem:10_4_B}: equal $(\nabla^2\tau, \Sign(\tau), \eps_\tau)$ plus interlacing determines $\tau$.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the B-type descent injectivity lemma.

nodes.name: Cor 10.10 D/B — PBPSet injectivity
nodes.statement: The map $\tau \mapsto (\nabla^2\tau, \Sign(\tau), \eps_\tau)$ is injective on $\PBP_\gamma(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$ for $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-\}$.
nodes.statement_short: tau -> (double descent, Sign, eps) is injective on PBP sets of types D, B+, B-.
nodes.label: cor:10_10

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Direct PBPSet-level wrapper of Prop.~\ref{prop:10_9_D} / \ref{prop:10_9_B}: convert the equality between subtype witnesses to PBP-level equality, then apply the injectivity theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Wrap the PBP-level injectivity propositions at the PBPSet subtype level.

nodes.name: Tail class for D type
nodes.statement: The \emph{tail class} of $\tau \in \PBP_D$ is one of $\{\mathrm{DD}, \mathrm{RC}, \mathrm{SS}\}$ determined by the tail symbol (Def.~\ref{def:tail}): $x_\tau = d$ gives $\mathrm{DD}$, $x_\tau \in \{r, c\}$ gives $\mathrm{RC}$, $x_\tau = s$ gives $\mathrm{SS}$.
nodes.statement_short: Tail class DD, RC or SS of a D-type PBP, read off from the tail symbol.
nodes.label: def:tailClass_D

nodes.name: countPBP\_D — recursion on D-type dp
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{countPBP\_D}(dp) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ is a triple $(n_{\mathrm{DD}}, n_{\mathrm{RC}}, n_{\mathrm{SS}})$ counting PBPs by tail class. Base case: $dp = []$ gives $(0, 0, 0)$ (or $(1, 0, 0)$ for the empty orbit, depending on the initial convention; see the Lean definition). Step: remove the first part of $dp$, recursively count on the remaining orbit, and combine via descent relations (Prop~\ref{prop:10_8_C_prim}, Prop~\ref{prop:10_8_C_bal}, or the balanced D split). $\mathrm{tripleSum}(n_{\mathrm{DD}}, n_{\mathrm{RC}}, n_{\mathrm{SS}}) := n_{\mathrm{DD}} + n_{\mathrm{RC}} + n_{\mathrm{SS}}$ is the total count.
nodes.statement_short: Recursive triple counting D-type PBPs by tail class, built by removing parts of dp and descent relations; tripleSum totals it.
nodes.label: def:countPBP_D

nodes.name: countPBP\_B — recursion on B-type dp
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{countPBP\_B}(dp) \in \mathbb{N}^3$ via analogous recursion, using the M$\to$B descent (Prop~10.8 M) plus recursion to D on a shifted shape.
nodes.label: def:countPBP_B

nodes.name: countPBP\_C — recursion on C-type dp
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{countPBP\_C}(dp) \in \mathbb{N}$ via descent to D: \[ \mathrm{countPBP\_C}(dp) = \begin{cases} \text{(primitive formula)} & \mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \geq \mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \\ n_{\mathrm{DD}} + n_{\mathrm{RC}} & \text{balanced} \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: C-type count via descent to D: primitive formula or DD+RC in the balanced case.
nodes.label: def:countPBP_C

nodes.name: countPBP\_M — recursion on M-type dp
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{countPBP\_M}(dp) \in \mathbb{N}$ via descent to B.
nodes.label: def:countPBP_M

nodes.name: Prop 10.11 B — counting for B type
nodes.statement: For any valid B-type dual partition $dp$ with shape $(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$ derived from $dp$: \[ |\PBP_{B^+}(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| + |\PBP_{B^-}(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = \mathrm{tripleSum}\big(\mathrm{countPBP\_B}(dp)\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Sum of B+ and B- PBP counts for a valid B-type dual partition equals tripleSum of countPBP_B.
assumptions: For any valid B-type dual partition $dp$ with shape $(\mu_P, \mu_Q)$ derived from $dp$
nodes.label: prop:10_11_B

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Joint induction on the ``Total'', ``A1'', ``A3'' components following the B-type lifting structure (see \texttt{CorrespondenceB.lean}, main theorem \texttt{card\_B\_combined}). The balanced cases use Prop~\ref{prop:10_8_M_bal} and a fiber decomposition of $\PBP_{B^\pm}$ along bottom-$\mathcal{Q}$ paint. Primitive cases use Prop~\ref{prop:10_8_M_prim} and the M-type balanced bijection together with induction hypothesis on the shifted $\mu_P$.
nodes.statement_short: Joint induction on the B-type lifting structure. Balanced cases use Prop 10.8 M balanced plus a fiber decomposition; primitive cases use Prop 10.8 M primitive.

nodes.name: Prop 10.11 D — counting for D type
nodes.statement: For any valid D-type dual partition $dp$: \[ |\PBP_D(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = \mathrm{tripleSum}\big(\mathrm{countPBP\_D}(dp)\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: D-type PBP count for a valid dual partition equals tripleSum of countPBP_D.
assumptions: For any valid D-type dual partition $dp$
nodes.label: prop:10_11_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By induction on $dp$. Base $dp = []$: both sides zero. Inductive step: split $\PBP_D$ along the first-column structure; each sub-class (DD/RC/SS) has a bijection to a lower-level count via the double-descent recursion, which by IH equals $\mathrm{tripleSum}(\mathrm{countPBP\_D}(\mathrm{tail}(dp)))$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on dp, splitting by tail class and using the double-descent recursion.

nodes.name: Prop 10.12 C — counting for C type
nodes.statement: For any valid C-type dual partition $dp$ (with $dp \neq []$): \[ |\PBP_C(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = \mathrm{countPBP\_C}(dp). \]
nodes.statement_short: C-type PBP count equals countPBP_C(dp).
assumptions: For any valid C-type dual partition $dp$ (with $dp \neq []$)
nodes.label: prop:10_12_C

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For $\mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \geq \mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$: apply Prop.~\ref{prop:10_8_C_prim} to reduce to $\PBP_D$; then invoke Prop.~\ref{prop:10_11_D}. For balanced: Prop.~\ref{prop:10_8_C_bal} gives $\mathrm{DD} + \mathrm{RC}$ of the next-level D count.
nodes.statement_short: Case split primitive/balanced; reduce to D-type via Prop 10.8 and apply the D-type count.

nodes.name: Prop 10.12 M — counting for M type
nodes.statement: For any valid M-type dual partition $dp$: \[ |\PBP_M(\mu_P, \mu_Q)| = \mathrm{countPBP\_M}(dp). \]
nodes.statement_short: M-type PBP count equals countPBP_M(dp).
assumptions: For any valid M-type dual partition $dp$
nodes.label: prop:10_12_M

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For $\mu_P.\mathrm{colLen}(0) > \mu_Q.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$: Prop.~\ref{prop:10_8_M_prim} reduces to $B^+ + B^-$, both settled by Prop.~\ref{prop:10_11_B}. Balanced: Prop.~\ref{prop:10_8_M_bal}.
nodes.statement_short: Case split primitive/balanced; reduce to B-type counts via Prop 10.8 M and Prop 10.11 B.

nodes.name: Unconditional status of the counting formulas
nodes.statement:
The counting recursion formulas (\ref{prop:10_11_B}, \ref{prop:10_11_D},
\ref{prop:10_12_C}, \ref{prop:10_12_M}) are \textbf{fully unconditional in the
following sense}: the hypotheses are only shape/dual-partition legality
(\texttt{SortedGE}, parity, positivity, shape match), all of which are
defining properties of ``valid B/D/C/M dual partition''. No auxiliary proof
object (ACResult, ILS, L, twist equality) is needed.
nodes.statement_short: The counting theorems need only shape/dual-partition legality hypotheses, no auxiliary proof objects.

nodes.name: Marked Young Diagrams (MYD)
nodes.statement:
Integer List Sequences (ILS)
are the computational representation of Marked Young Diagrams (MYDs).
nodes.section: 7 Integer List Sequences and MYD Operations

nodes.name: ILS
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{ILS} := \mathrm{List}(\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z})$. The $i$-th entry (0-indexed) represents row $i + 1$ of the associated MYD, carrying a mark $(p_i, q_i) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$.
nodes.statement_short: An ILS is a list of integer pairs, entry i giving the mark of row i+1 of an MYD.
nodes.label: def:ILS

nodes.name: Row contribution to signature
nodes.statement: (Paper Eq.~(9.10).) For row $i$ (0-indexed) of length $\ell = i + 1$, let $h := \lfloor \ell / 2 \rfloor$ and $r := \ell \bmod 2$. The row contribution is \[ \mathrm{signRow}(i,\ (p, q)) := \big(|p|(h + r) + |q| h,\ |q|(h + r) + |p| h\big). \] Concretely: odd-length rows (i.e., $\ell$ odd, $r = 1$) get extra $|p|$ / $|q|$ contribution.
nodes.statement_short: Signature contribution of a marked row of length i+1 (paper Eq. 9.10).
nodes.label: def:signRow

nodes.name: ILS signature $\Sign(\mathcal{E})$
nodes.statement: $\Sign(\mathcal{E}) := \sum_{i} \mathrm{signRow}(i, \mathcal{E}[i]) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$. Since \texttt{signRow} is a sum of $|p|, |q|$ (non-negative integer) contributions, $\Sign(\mathcal{E}).1, \Sign(\mathcal{E}).2 \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Signature of an ILS: sum of row contributions; nonnegative.
nodes.label: def:sign

nodes.name: First-column row contribution
nodes.statement: (Paper Eq.~(9.12).) Per-row contribution to the first-column signature: \[ \mathrm{firstColSignRow}(i,\ (p, q)) := \begin{cases} (|p|, |q|) & i\text{ even} \\ (|q|, |p|) & i\text{ odd (swap!)} \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: First-column contribution of a row: (|p|,|q|), swapped for odd row index (Eq. 9.12).
nodes.label: def:firstColSignRow

nodes.name: First-column signature $\mathrm{fcSign}$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}) := \sum_i \mathrm{firstColSignRow}(i, \mathcal{E}[i])$.
nodes.label: def:firstColSign

nodes.name: Sign twist $\otimes (\eps^+, \eps^-)$
nodes.statement: (Paper Eq.~(9.15).) For $(\eps^+, \eps^-) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ (in practice $\{\pm 1\}^2$), acts only on odd-length rows ($\ell = i + 1$ odd, $i$ even): \[ \mathrm{twistBDRow}(i,\ \eps^+, \eps^-)(p, q) := \begin{cases} (p, q) & \ell\text{ even} \\ (\eps^{+\,h + 1} \eps^{-\,h}\, p,\ \eps^{-\,h + 1} \eps^{+\,h}\, q) & \ell\text{ odd, } h = i / 2. \end{cases} \] Common cases: \begin{itemize} \item $(1, -1)$: sign twist $\otimes 1^{+-}$ (B/D post-twist when $\eps_\tau = 1$). \item $(-1, -1)$: det twist (C/M pre-twist when $\eps_\wp = 1$). \item $(1, 1)$: identity. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Sign twist by (eps+, eps-) acting on odd-length rows (paper Eq. 9.15); special cases sign twist, det twist, identity.
nodes.label: def:twistBD

nodes.name: Character twist $T^j$
nodes.statement: (Paper Eq.~(9.16)--(9.17).) For $j \in \mathbb{Z}$, $T^j$ negates the pair at row index $i$ iff $j$ is odd and $(i + 1) \bmod 4 = 2$: \[ \mathrm{charTwistCMRow}(j, i)(p, q) := \begin{cases} (-p, -q) & j\text{ odd and } (i + 1) \bmod 4 = 2 \\ (p, q) & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]
nodes.statement_short: Character twist T^j negates rows with (i+1) mod 4 = 2 when j is odd (paper Eq. 9.16-9.17).
nodes.label: def:charTwistCM

nodes.name: $T^2 = \mathrm{id}$
nodes.statement: The character twist is an involution.
nodes.statement_short: The character twist T is an involution.
nodes.label: lem:T_squared

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Per-row: each entry is negated twice (identity) or left unchanged; both yield identity.
nodes.statement_short: Row-wise: negating twice or not at all is the identity.

nodes.name: Augmentation $\oplus (p_0, q_0)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{augment}((p_0, q_0), \mathcal{E}) := (p_0, q_0) :: \mathcal{E}$. Prepend at position~0 (shift existing rows up by~1).
nodes.label: def:augment

nodes.name: Truncation $\Lambda_{(p_0, q_0)}$
nodes.statement: Subtract $(p_0, q_0)$ from the first entry, defined when the containment condition $\mathcal{E}[0] \supseteq (p_0, q_0)$ holds (both components non-negative and $|\mathcal{E}[0]_i| \geq |(p_0, q_0)_i|$).
nodes.statement_short: Truncation subtracts (p0,q0) from the first entry when the containment condition holds.
nodes.label: def:truncate

nodes.name: Twist preserves signature
nodes.statement: $\Sign(\mathcal{E} \otimes (\eps^+, \eps^-)) = \Sign(\mathcal{E})$ and $\Sign(T^j \mathcal{E}) = \Sign(\mathcal{E})$.
nodes.statement_short: Sign twists and character twists preserve the ILS signature.
nodes.label: lem:twist_sign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $\Sign$ uses $|p|, |q|$, which are unchanged by sign twists.
nodes.statement_short: Sign uses absolute values, which sign twists leave unchanged.

nodes.name: Twist preserves first-column signature
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E} \otimes (\eps^+, \eps^-)) = \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E})$ and $\mathrm{fcSign}(T^j \mathcal{E}) = \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E})$.
nodes.statement_short: Sign twists and character twists preserve the first-column signature.
nodes.label: lem:twist_fcSign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $\Sign$ is defined from $|p|, |q|$ via \texttt{signRow}; the twists act only by signs $\pm 1$, which absolute values ignore.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute values ignore the signs the twists introduce.

nodes.name: Augmentation signature formula
nodes.statement: For $p_0, q_0 \geq 0$: \[ \Sign\big((p_0, q_0) :: \mathcal{E}\big) = \big(p_0 + \Sign(\mathcal{E}).1 + \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).2,\ q_0 + \Sign(\mathcal{E}).2 + \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).1\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Signature of an augmented ILS: new pair plus old signature plus swapped first-column signature.
nodes.label: lem:augment_sign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Same argument as Lemma~\ref{lem:twist_sign}: $\mathrm{fcSign}$ per Eq.~(9.12) uses absolute values, so sign twists and $T^j$ preserve it.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as for twist preservation: fcSign uses absolute values.

nodes.name: Theta lift $\hat\vartheta$
nodes.statement: Four variants (paper Eq.~(9.29)--(9.30)): \begin{itemize} \item $\hat\vartheta_{CD} : \MYD_C \to \MYD_D$ (single branch): $\mathcal{E} \mapsto T^j(\mathrm{augment}((p, q), \mathcal{E}))$. \item $\hat\vartheta_{DC} : \MYD_D \to \MYD_C$ (two branches: standard with $\mathrm{augment}((n, n), \mathcal{E})$; split with $\mathrm{augment}((-1, -1), \Lambda(\mathcal{E}))$). \item $\hat\vartheta_{BM}, \hat\vartheta_{MB}$ analogous. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Four theta-lift variants on MYDs/ILS, built from augmentation, truncation and the character twist (paper Eq. 9.29-9.30).
nodes.label: def:thetaLift

nodes.name: Theta lift signature preservation
nodes.statement: For each theta-lift direction with target $(p, q)$ satisfying the standard-case condition ($p - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).1 - \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).2 \geq 0$, etc.): $\Sign(\hat\vartheta(\mathcal{E})) = (p, q)$ (or $(n, n)$ in D$\to$C split).
nodes.statement_short: Theta lifts in the standard case produce ILS with the target signature (p,q).
assumptions: For each theta-lift direction with target $(p, q)$ satisfying the standard-case condition ($p - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).1 - \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).2 \geq 0$, etc.)
nodes.label: thm:thetaLift_sign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $\Sign((p_0, q_0) :: \mathcal{E})$ evaluates \texttt{signRow} at the new index~0 (contributing $(|p_0|, |q_0|)$) and shifts every existing row index by~1, which adds its $\mathrm{firstColSignRow}$ contribution.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate signRow at the new row 0 and account for the index shift of existing rows.

nodes.name: Theta lift first-column signature
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{fcSign}(\hat\vartheta(\mathcal{E})) = (p - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).1,\ q - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).2)$ (the key \emph{firstColSign invariant}).
nodes.statement_short: First-column signature of a theta lift equals target minus source signature (firstColSign invariant).
nodes.label: thm:thetaLift_fcSign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Each $\hat\vartheta_\bullet$ is of the form $T^j(\mathrm{augment}((p, q), \mathcal{E}))$ (or similar with $(n, n)$ or $(-1, -1)$). Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:augment_sign} then Lemma~\ref{lem:twist_sign} for the $T^j$ step.
nodes.statement_short: Write each theta lift as T^j of an augmentation; apply the augmentation signature lemma then twist invariance.

nodes.name: Theta lift first-entry formula
nodes.statement: The first entry of $\hat\vartheta(\mathcal{E})$ is $(p - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).1 - \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).2,\ q - \Sign(\mathcal{E}).2 - \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{E}).1)$.
nodes.statement_short: First entry of a theta lift equals target minus source signature minus swapped first-column signature.
nodes.label: thm:thetaLift_first_entry

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \texttt{thetaLift\_*\_firstColSign} follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:twist_fcSign} for the $T^j$ step and the observation that $\mathrm{augment}((p_0, q_0), \cdot)$ shifts every row's first-column contribution.
nodes.statement_short: Twist invariance of fcSign plus the row-shift effect of augmentation.

nodes.name: AC base case
nodes.statement: When $|\check{\mathcal{O}}| = 0$ the base $\mathcal{L}_\tau$ is determined by $\gamma$: \[ \mathrm{AC.base}\,\gamma = \begin{cases} [(1,\ [(1, 0)])] & \gamma = B^+ \\ [(1,\ [(0, -1)])] & \gamma = B^- \\ [(1,\ [])] & \gamma \in \{C, D, M\}. \end{cases} \] (Each list entry is an \texttt{ACResult} branch: \texttt{(coeff, ILS)}.)
nodes.statement_short: Base associated-cycle value for the empty orbit, depending on the root type.
nodes.label: def:AC_base

nodes.name: AC step — single recursion step
nodes.statement: Given a source $\mathrm{ACResult}$ and target $\gamma$, together with parameters $(p, q, \eps_\tau, \eps_\wp) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 \times \{0, 1\}^2$, define: \begin{itemize} \item If $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-\}$ (no C/M pre-twist): \[ \mathrm{AC.step} = \begin{cases} (\mathrm{source.thetaLift}\,\gamma\,p\,q)\otimes(1, -1) & \eps_\tau = 1 \\ \mathrm{source.thetaLift}\,\gamma\,p\,q & \eps_\tau = 0 \end{cases} \] \item If $\gamma \in \{C, M\}$: first pre-twist the source by $\otimes(-1, -1)^{\eps_\wp}$, then theta lift. \end{itemize} The resulting \texttt{ACResult} carries all branches.
nodes.statement_short: One AC recursion step: theta lift of the source, with B/D post-twist when eps_tau=1 or C/M pre-twist when eps_wp=1.
nodes.label: def:AC_step

nodes.name: AC fold — chain of AC.step
nodes.statement: Given a descent chain \texttt{chain : List ACStepData}, inductively apply \texttt{AC.step} from \texttt{AC.base} to get the final \texttt{ACResult}, yielding $\mathcal{L}_\tau$ when the chain is $\tau$'s descent sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate AC.step along a descent chain from AC.base to get L_tau.
nodes.label: def:AC_fold

nodes.name: AC.step preserves signature ($\gamma = D$)
nodes.statement: Every branch of the output has $\Sign = (p, q)$: \[ \forall r \in \mathrm{AC.step}_{D}(\mathrm{source}, p, q, \eps_\tau, \eps_\wp),\quad \Sign(r.2) = (p, q). \]
nodes.statement_short: Every branch of AC.step for gamma=D has signature (p,q).
nodes.label: thm:AC_step_sign_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Unfold \texttt{AC.step} for $\gamma = D$: it is \texttt{thetaLift\_CD} followed (optionally) by \texttt{twistBD}. Both preserve $\Sign$; the initial value is $(p, q)$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:thetaLift_sign}.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold AC.step as theta lift plus optional twist; both preserve Sign.

nodes.name: AC.step preserves signature (all $\gamma$)
nodes.statement: Parallel statements for $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-, C, M\}$.
nodes.statement_short: AC.step preserves signature for gamma in {B+, B-, C, M}.
nodes.label: thm:AC_step_sign_all

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Parallel argument to the D case using the corresponding \texttt{thetaLift} / twist preservation for each $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-, C, M\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Parallel to the D case using the corresponding theta-lift and twist preservation.

nodes.name: AC.base signature
nodes.statement: $\Sign(\mathrm{AC.base}\,\gamma) = (0, 0)$ for $\gamma \in \{C, D, M\}$; $\Sign(\mathrm{AC.base}\,B^+) = (1, 0)$; $\Sign(\mathrm{AC.base}\,B^-) = (0, 1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Signatures of AC.base: (0,0) for C,D,M; (1,0) for B+; (0,1) for B-.
nodes.label: thm:AC_base_sign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By direct inspection of each case: \texttt{AC.base}$\,B^+ = [(1, [(1, 0)])]$ has $\Sign = (1, 0)$; $B^-$ gives $(0, 1)$; $C, D, M$ have empty ILS with $\Sign = (0, 0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Direct inspection of each case.

nodes.name: firstColSign diff invariant
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}_\tau = \mathrm{AC.fold}\,\gamma\,(\mathrm{descent\ chain})$, with the descent chain producing signatures $\Sign(\mathcal{L}_\tau)$ and $\Sign(\mathcal{L}_{\tau''})$ at successive levels. Then \[ \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{L}_\tau) = \Sign(\mathcal{L}_\tau) - \Sign(\mathcal{L}_{\tau''}). \] Equivalently: \[ \mathrm{fcSign}(\mathcal{L}_\tau) = (p_\tau - p_{\tau''},\ q_\tau - q_{\tau''}). \]
nodes.statement_short: fcSign of L_tau equals Sign(L_tau) minus Sign(L_tau'') along the descent chain.
nodes.label: thm:fcSign_diff

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By induction on the descent chain length. Base: $\mathrm{fcSign}(\mathrm{AC.base}) = \Sign(\mathrm{AC.base})$ (\texttt{AC.base\_firstColSign\_eq\_sign}). Step: Given $\mathrm{fcSign}(\text{prev}) = \Sign(\text{prev}) - \Sign(\text{prev}')$, the post-twist and theta-lift formulas (Thm~\ref{thm:thetaLift_fcSign}, Lem~\ref{lem:twist_fcSign}) give \[ \mathrm{fcSign}(\text{curr}) = (\text{current } p - \Sign(\text{prev}).1,\ \text{current } q - \Sign(\text{prev}).2) \] $= (p_\tau - p_{\tau''},\ q_\tau - q_{\tau''})$ since the current parameters are $\Sign(\tau) = (p_\tau, q_\tau)$ and the previous source has $\Sign = \Sign(\tau'')$ by IH.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the descent chain length. The step uses the theta-lift and twist fcSign formulas with the IH.

nodes.name: AC.step fcSign invariant — per $\gamma$
nodes.statement: For each $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-, C, M\}$, every branch of $\mathrm{AC.step}$'s output has $\mathrm{fcSign}(r.2) = (p - \mathrm{prev\_sig}.1,\ q - \mathrm{prev\_sig}.2)$ where $\mathrm{prev\_sig} = \Sign(\text{source})$.
nodes.statement_short: Every branch of AC.step has fcSign = (p,q) minus source signature, for each root type.
assumptions: For each $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-, C, M\}$
nodes.label: thm:AC_step_fcSign

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For each $\gamma$ the \texttt{AC.step} output is a lifted ILS $(p_0, q_0) :: \mathcal{E}'$ whose first-column signature equals $(p - \mathrm{src\_sig}.1, q - \mathrm{src\_sig}.2)$ by the augment + twist formulas (Theorem~\ref{thm:thetaLift_fcSign}, Lemma~\ref{lem:twist_fcSign}).
nodes.statement_short: AC.step output is an augmented ILS; apply the augment and twist fcSign formulas.

nodes.name: ACResult.postTwist first entry
nodes.statement: After the B/D post-twist $\otimes(1, -1)$ (when $\eps_\tau = 1$), the first entry of every branch transforms by $(a, b) \mapsto (a, -b)$.
nodes.statement_short: The B/D post-twist maps the first entry (a,b) of each branch to (a,-b).
conclusions: the first entry of every branch transforms by $(a, b) \mapsto (a, -b)$
nodes.label: thm:postTwist_first_entry

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $(a, b) \otimes (1, -1)$ maps $(a, b) \mapsto (a, -b)$ when $\eps_\tau = 1$ (by the definition of \texttt{twistBD} on the first row, which is odd-length), and is the identity otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: By the definition of twistBD on the odd-length first row.

nodes.name: MultiplicityFree
nodes.statement: An $\mathrm{ACResult}$ is \emph{multiplicity free} if no two branches carry the same ILS.
differentia: no two branches carry the same ILS
nodes.label: def:mfree

nodes.name: Prop 11.7 — $\mathcal{L}_\tau$ is multiplicity free
nodes.statement: The AC output $\mathcal{L}_\tau \in \mathbb{Z}[\MYD_\star]$ is multiplicity free.
nodes.statement_short: The associated cycle L_tau is multiplicity free.
nodes.label: prop:11_7

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By induction. Base: \texttt{AC.base}'s single branch is trivially multiplicity free. Inductive step: the four operations (sign twist, $T$, augmentation, truncation) are either injective or extend uniformly across branches, and AC.step preserves distinct ILS's by tracking sign/fcSign differences.
nodes.statement_short: Induction along AC steps: base has one branch; operations are injective or uniform across branches.

nodes.name: Tail length $k$
nodes.statement: For $\tau \in \PBP_D$ with $\mathcal{P}$ col~0 longer than $\mathcal{Q}$ col~0, the \emph{tail length} is \[ k := \tau.\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) - \tau.\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0). \] Equivalently $k = (\mathbf{r}_1(\check{\mathcal{O}}) - \mathbf{r}_2(\check{\mathcal{O}}))/2 + 1$ via the BV dual correspondence.
nodes.statement_short: Tail length k = colLen_P(0) - colLen_Q(0), equivalently (r_1 - r_2)/2 + 1.
nodes.label: def:tailLen

nodes.name: Tail symbol $x_\tau$ and top-of-tail symbol $x_1$
nodes.statement: For D type, the tail is the sequence of cells $(\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0), 0),\ (\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) + 1, 0),\ \ldots,\ (\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) - 1, 0)$ in $\mathcal{P}$'s column~0. We write: \begin{itemize} \item $x_\tau := \mathcal{P}_\tau(\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) - 1, 0)$ — \emph{bottom} tail cell (maximum $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ by layer monotonicity). \item $x_1 := \mathcal{P}_\tau(\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0), 0)$ — \emph{top} tail cell (minimum $\mathrm{layerOrd}$). \end{itemize} For B type: analogous symbols in $\mathcal{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: The tail is the run of P's column-0 cells below Q's column 0; x_tau is its bottom symbol and x_1 its top.
nodes.label: def:tailSymbol

nodes.name: Tail signature $\mathrm{tailSig}(\tau) = (p_{\tau_t}, q_{\tau_t})$
nodes.statement: \[ \mathrm{tailSig}(\tau) := \sum_{i = \tau.\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0)}^{\tau.\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) - 1} \mathrm{tailContrib}(\mathcal{P}_\tau(i, 0)). \] Each cell contributes $\mathrm{tailContrib}$ (Def.~\ref{def:tailContrib}); components sum to~$2$ per cell.
nodes.statement_short: Tail signature: sum of tailContrib over tail cells.
nodes.label: def:tailSignature

nodes.name: Tail signature sum identity
nodes.statement: $p_{\tau_t} + q_{\tau_t} = 2k$ where $k$ is the tail length.
nodes.statement_short: Tail signature components sum to twice the tail length.
nodes.label: lem:tailSig_sum

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Each tail cell contributes $\mathrm{tailContrib}$ with $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).1 + \mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).2 = 2$ for every symbol $\sigma$. Summing over the $k$ tail cells gives $p_{\tau_t} + q_{\tau_t} = 2k$.
nodes.statement_short: Each tail cell contributes total 2; sum over k cells.

nodes.name: Tail signature non-negativity
nodes.statement: $p_{\tau_t} \geq 0$ and $q_{\tau_t} \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Tail signature components are nonnegative.
nodes.label: lem:tailSig_nonneg

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Each $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma)$ has non-negative components; the sum is non-negative in both components.
nodes.statement_short: Each tailContrib is nonnegative.

nodes.name: Prop 11.3 — characterisation of $x_\tau$, $x_1$ via signatures and $\eps$
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) > \mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item $\eps_\tau = 0 \iff x_\tau = d$. \item $p_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff x_\tau = s \iff $ every tail cell is $s$. \item $q_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff $ every tail cell is $r$ $\iff x_1 = r$ and $x_\tau = r$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Characterises x_tau = d, all-s tails and all-r tails via eps and the tail signature.
conclusions: $p_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff x_\tau = s \iff $ every tail cell is $s$.
$q_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff $ every tail cell is $r$ $\iff x_1 = r$ and $x_\tau = r$.
nodes.label: lem:11_3

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \textbf{(1)} By layer monotonicity in column~0, a symbol $d$ (with maximal $\mathrm{layerOrd} = 4$) can only appear at the bottom. Conversely, $\eps_\tau = 0$ iff $d$ is present somewhere in column~0, which by monotonicity forces it to the bottom, i.e., $x_\tau = d$. \textbf{(2)} $p_{\tau_t} = \sum_i \mathrm{tailContrib}(x_i).p$, and $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).p = 0$ only for $\sigma = s$. Combined with the non-negativity of each term, $p_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff $ every tail cell is $s$. Now the equivalence ``every tail cell is $s$'' $\iff$ $x_\tau = s$ follows from layer monotonicity: $x_\tau = s$ means the $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ at the bottom is $1$; all cells above have $\mathrm{layerOrd} \leq 1$; combined with non-dot (every tail cell is non-$\bullet$ by $\mathrm{dot\_match}$), every cell has $\mathrm{layerOrd} = 1$, i.e., equals $s$. \textbf{(3)} $q_{\tau_t} = \sum_i \mathrm{tailContrib}(x_i).q$, and $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).q = 0$ only for $\sigma = r$. So $q_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff$ every tail cell is $r$. The second equivalence: ``every tail cell is $r$'' $\iff$ $x_1 = r$ and $x_\tau = r$. Layer monotonicity gives $\mathrm{layerOrd}(x_1) \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_\tau)$ for every tail cell $x_i$. If $x_1 = x_\tau = r$ (both equal $2$), then every $x_i$ has $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ sandwiched as $2 \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) \leq 2$, so $\mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) = 2$, i.e., $x_i = r$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: Part-by-part: layer monotonicity in column 0 plus the tailContrib table.

nodes.name: Remark
nodes.statement: Unlike part~(2), part~(3) cannot be stated purely in terms of the bottom symbol $x_\tau$: the tail can have an $s$ cell above an $r$ bottom (layer orders $1 \leq 2$), giving $q_{\tau_t} = 2 \neq 0$. The correct statement requires either every tail cell to be $r$ or, equivalently, both $x_1$ and $x_\tau$ to be $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (3) cannot be phrased via the bottom symbol alone: an s above an r bottom gives q_t = 2.

nodes.name: D-type signature sum
nodes.statement: For $\tau \in \PBP_D$: \[ p_\tau + q_\tau = 2\cdot|\tau|. \] (Each cell contributes exactly $2$ to the total $p + q$.)
nodes.statement_short: For D-type PBPs, p_tau + q_tau = 2|tau|.
nodes.label: lem:sig_sum_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Combine $p_\tau = \#_\bullet + \#_s + 2\#_r + \#_c + \#_d$ and the symmetric expression for $q_\tau$. Since $\mathcal{Q}$ is all $\bullet$ for D type, the non-dot counts come from $\mathcal{P}$ only, and $p_\tau + q_\tau = 2 \cdot |\mathcal{P}| + 2 \cdot |\mathcal{Q}| = 2|\tau|$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the signature formulas; Q is all dots for D type so each cell counts twice.

nodes.name: Tail residual identity
nodes.statement: For $\tau \in \PBP_D$: \[ p_{\tau_t} + q_{\tau_t} = 2 \cdot \mathbf{c}_1(\mathcal{O}) - 2 \cdot \mathbf{c}_2(\mathcal{O}). \]
nodes.statement_short: Tail signature sum equals 2c_1 - 2c_2.
nodes.label: lem:residual_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $k = \mathbf{c}_1 - \mathbf{c}_2$ by the BV dual column-length relations (specifically $\mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) = \mathbf{c}_1$, $\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) = \mathbf{c}_2$). Apply Lem.~\ref{lem:tailSig_sum}.
nodes.statement_short: k = c_1 - c_2 by BV dual column relations; apply the tail signature sum lemma.

nodes.name: Prop 11.4 D — signature decomposition (Eq 11.7)
nodes.statement_short: Signature of a D-type PBP splits as (c_2,c_2) + Sign(double descent) + tail signature.
nodes.label: prop:11_4

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Decompose $\mathcal{P}$'s cells into three groups: \begin{enumerate} \item \emph{Column~0 below $\mathcal{Q}$'s col~0} ($i < \mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$): these are all $\bullet$ by the dot\_match axiom, contributing $\mathbf{c}_2(\mathcal{O}) \cdot (1, 1) / 2$ per cell... actually the direct expansion gives $\mathbf{c}_2(\mathcal{O})$ to both $p$ and $q$ via the $\bullet$ contribution to the signature formula. \item \emph{Columns $\geq 1$}: these match $\nabla^2\tau$'s columns exactly (up to shift), contributing $\Sign(\nabla^2\tau)$ (on a shifted shape). \item \emph{Tail cells} ($\mathcal{Q}.\mathrm{colLen}(0) \leq i < \mathcal{P}.\mathrm{colLen}(0)$ in column~0): contribute $\mathrm{tailSig}(\tau)$ by Def.~\ref{def:tailSignature}. \end{enumerate} Uses \texttt{countSym\_split}, \texttt{col0\_dot\_below\_Q\_D}, \texttt{Q\_countSym\_eq\_zero\_of\_D}, and the per-component $\mathrm{tailContrib}$ table.
nodes.statement_short: Split P's cells into column 0 above the tail, columns >=1 and the tail; sum contributions.

nodes.name: Setup for Lemma 11.5
nodes.statement:
Let $\star \in \{B, D\}$ and assume $\mathbf{r}_2(\check{\mathcal{O}}) > \mathbf{r}_3(\check{\mathcal{O}})$
(the \emph{primitive case}). Set:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\tau \in \PBP_\star(\check{\mathcal{O}})$ (outer PBP).
  \item $\tau' = \nabla\tau \in \PBP_{\star'}(\check{\mathcal{O}}')$ (single descent; $\star' = C$ for $\star = D$, $\star' = \tilde{C}$ for $\star \in \{B^\pm\}$).
  \item $\tau'' = \nabla^2\tau = \nabla(\tau') \in \PBP_\star(\check{\mathcal{O}}'')$ (double descent).
  \item $\tau_t \in \PBP_D(\check{\mathcal{O}}_t)$ (tail PBP).
  \item $n_0 := (\mathbf{c}_1(\mathcal{O}') - \mathbf{c}_2(\mathcal{O}')) / 2$ (the inner augmentation parameter).
  \item $\mathcal{L}_\tau, \mathcal{L}_{\tau''}$ denote the AC results.
\end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: In the primitive case set tau' and tau'' as single and double descents, tau_t the tail PBP, and n_0 the inner augmentation parameter.

nodes.name: $n_0$ in terms of $\mathcal{O}$
nodes.statement:
By the shape relations $\mathbf{c}_i(\mathcal{O}') = \mathbf{c}_{i+1}(\mathcal{O})$, we have
$n_0 = (\mathbf{c}_2(\mathcal{O}) - \mathbf{c}_3(\mathcal{O}))/2$.

nodes.name: Lemma 11.5 D (primitive case, ILS-level, unconditional)
nodes.statement: Given an ILS $E$ (intended as $\mathcal{L}_{\tau''}$) with the firstColSign invariant \[ \mathrm{fcSign}(E) = (\Sign(E).1 - n_{\mathrm{prev}},\ \Sign(E).2 - n_{\mathrm{prev}}) \] and target tail signature $(p_t, q_t)$ satisfying \[ p_\tau - 2 n_{\mathrm{inner}} + \Sign(E).2 = p_t,\quad q_\tau - 2 n_{\mathrm{inner}} + \Sign(E).1 = q_t, \] define $n_0 := n_{\mathrm{inner}} - \Sign(E).1 - \Sign(E).2 + n_{\mathrm{prev}}$ and $E_{\mathrm{inner}} := T^{\gamma_1}\big(E \oplus (n_0, n_0)\big)$. Then: \begin{align*} p_\tau - \Sign(E_{\mathrm{inner}}).1 - \mathrm{fcSign}(E_{\mathrm{inner}}).2 &= p_t, \\ q_\tau - \Sign(E_{\mathrm{inner}}).2 - \mathrm{fcSign}(E_{\mathrm{inner}}).1 &= q_t. \end{align*} These are the ``outer augment'' parameters consumed by the outer C$\to$D or M$\to$B lift.
nodes.statement_short: ILS-level two-step AC identity: the inner augmentation gives the outer augment parameters equal to the tail signature.
nodes.label: lem:11_5_D_ILS

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 1 — unfold sign and fcSign of $E_{\mathrm{inner}}$.} $T^\gamma$ preserves both sign and fcSign (Lem~\ref{lem:twist_sign}, \ref{lem:twist_fcSign}), so we may work with $F := E \oplus (n_0, n_0) = (n_0, n_0) :: E$. By Lem~\ref{lem:augment_sign} (for $n_0 \geq 0$): \begin{align*} \Sign(F) &= (n_0 + \Sign(E).1 + \mathrm{fcSign}(E).2,\ n_0 + \Sign(E).2 + \mathrm{fcSign}(E).1). \\ \mathrm{fcSign}(F) &= (n_0 + \mathrm{fcSign}(E).2,\ n_0 + \mathrm{fcSign}(E).1) \end{align*} using the cons formula for fcSign (the swap is due to parity index shift, Eq.~(9.12)). Substituting $\mathrm{fcSign}(E) = (\Sign(E).1 - n_{\mathrm{prev}},\ \Sign(E).2 - n_{\mathrm{prev}})$: \begin{align*} \Sign(F).1 &= n_0 + \Sign(E).1 + \Sign(E).2 - n_{\mathrm{prev}} = n_{\mathrm{inner}} \\ \mathrm{fcSign}(F).2 &= n_0 + \Sign(E).1 - n_{\mathrm{prev}} = n_{\mathrm{inner}} - \Sign(E).2. \end{align*} where we used the definition $n_0 = n_{\mathrm{inner}} - \Sign(E).1 - \Sign(E).2 + n_{\mathrm{prev}}$. \textbf{Step 2 — substitute into the outer augment formula.} $p_\tau - \Sign(F).1 - \mathrm{fcSign}(F).2 = p_\tau - n_{\mathrm{inner}} - (n_{\mathrm{inner}} - \Sign(E).2) = p_\tau - 2 n_{\mathrm{inner}} + \Sign(E).2 = p_t$ (by hypothesis). The $q$-equation is symmetric.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold Sign and fcSign of the augmented ILS using twist invariance and the augmentation formula, then substitute.

nodes.name: Fact 1 — signature sum D
nodes.statement: $p_\tau + q_\tau = 2|\tau|$.
nodes.statement_short: Signature sum p+q = 2|tau| for D type (restated for the atomic discharge).
nodes.label: lem:fact1_sig_sum

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Same argument as Lemma~\ref{lem:sig_sum_D}: for D type $\mathcal{Q}$ is all $\bullet$, so the non-$\bullet$ counts come from $\mathcal{P}$ only; $p_\tau + q_\tau$ equals twice the total cell count.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as the D-type signature-sum lemma.

nodes.name: Fact 2 — descent cell-count definitional
nodes.statement: $|\tau| - \mathbf{c}_1 = $ single-descent cell count (by definition of cells - col 0).
nodes.statement_short: |tau| - c_1 is the cell count after one descent (definitional).
nodes.label: lem:fact2_descent

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Definitional: $|\tau| - \mathbf{c}_1(\mathcal{O})$ equals the cell count of $\tau$ minus the cells in $\mathcal{P}$'s column~0, which is the cell count after a single descent step.
nodes.statement_short: Definitional: removing column 0 of P.

nodes.name: Fact 3 — tail residual
nodes.statement: $p_{\tau_t} + q_{\tau_t} = 2 \mathbf{c}_1 - 2 \mathbf{c}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Tail residual p_t + q_t = 2c_1 - 2c_2 (restated).
nodes.label: lem:fact3_residual

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:residual_D}: applying \texttt{tailSig\_sum} ($p_t + q_t = 2k$) with $k = \mathbf{c}_1 - \mathbf{c}_2$ (BV dual column relation) gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the tail residual identity.

nodes.name: Lemma 11.5 atomic discharge at PBP level
nodes.statement: Given the canonical choices of $|\tau|, \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{c}_2,$ tail signatures, the three atomic cell-count hypotheses of \texttt{prop\_11\_5\_D\_atomic} are discharged automatically; the remaining inputs are: \begin{itemize} \item $(E, n_{\mathrm{prev}}, p_{\mathrm{prev}}, q_{\mathrm{prev}})$: an inner ILS + its Sign and prev-sig. \item $h_{\mathrm{fc}}, h_{\mathrm{sign}}$: firstColSign/Sign relations on $E$ (auto by AC.fold). \item $h_{\mathrm{prop11.4}}$: signature decomposition (Prop~\ref{prop:11_4}). \item $h_{n_0}$: $n_0 \geq 0$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: At PBP level the three atomic cell-count hypotheses of Lemma 11.5 discharge automatically, leaving listed inputs.
nodes.label: thm:11_5_atomic_pbp

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The three hypotheses of \texttt{prop\_11\_5\_D\_atomic} are discharged by Lemmas~\ref{lem:fact1_sig_sum}, \ref{lem:fact2_descent}, \ref{lem:fact3_residual} respectively; the remainder follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:11_5_D_ILS}.
nodes.statement_short: Discharge the hypotheses by Facts 1-3, then apply the ILS-level Lemma 11.5.

nodes.name: Lemma 11.6 D (AC-level, unconditional)
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma = D$ (no C/M pre-twist). For \texttt{source : ACResult} with uniform $\Sign = \mathrm{src\_sig}$ and uniform $\mathrm{fcSign} = \mathrm{src\_fcSig}$ satisfying the standard-case condition ($p - \mathrm{src\_sig}.1 - \mathrm{src\_fcSig}.2 \geq 0$, etc.): every branch $r \in \mathrm{AC.step}(\mathrm{source}, D, p, q, \eps_\tau, \eps_\wp)$ has \[ r.2.\mathrm{head?} = \mathrm{some}\big(p - \mathrm{src\_sig}.1 - \mathrm{src\_fcSig}.2,\ (-1)^{\eps_\tau}(q - \mathrm{src\_sig}.2 - \mathrm{src\_fcSig}.1)\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: For gamma=D, each branch of AC.step has first entry (p - sig.1 - fc.2, (-1)^eps (q - sig.2 - fc.1)).
nodes.label: lem:11_6_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Thm~\ref{thm:thetaLift_first_entry}, the first entry of $\hat\vartheta_{CD}(\mathrm{source})$ (standard case) is $(p - \mathrm{src\_sig}.1 - \mathrm{src\_fcSig}.2,\ q - \mathrm{src\_sig}.2 - \mathrm{src\_fcSig}.1)$. The post-twist $\otimes(1, -1)$ (when $\eps_\tau = 1$) maps $(a, b) \mapsto (a, -b)$ by Thm~\ref{thm:postTwist_first_entry}.

nodes.statement: Parallel statements for $\gamma \in \{B^+, B^-\}$, using $\hat\vartheta_{MB}$.

nodes.name: Proof

nodes.name: PBP-level Lemma 11.6
nodes.statement: At the PBP level, when $\mathrm{src\_sig} = \Sign(\tau'') = (p_{\tau''}, q_{\tau''})$ and $\mathrm{src\_fcSig} = \Sign(\tau'') - \Sign(\tau^{(4)})$, the first entry of $\mathcal{L}_\tau$ equals \[ \big(p_{\tau_t},\ (-1)^{\eps_\tau} q_{\tau_t}\big) \] by combining Lem~\ref{lem:11_6_D} with Prop~\ref{prop:11_4} (which gives $p_\tau - \mathbf{c}_2 - p_{\tau''} = p_{\tau_t}$).

nodes.name: Proof

nodes.name: Proof

nodes.name: SignTargetSet cardinality formula
nodes.statement: For $(p, q) \in \mathbb{N}^2$, the set $\{(\eps^+, \eps^-) \in \mathbb{Z}^2 : (\eps^+, \eps^-) \in \{(p, q), (p, -q), (-p, q), (-p, -q)\}\}$ has cardinality $4m + 4$ when $p > 0, q > 0$ (after suitable deduplication for $p = 0$ or $q = 0$).
nodes.statement_short: The set of sign variants (+-p, +-q) has the stated cardinality.
nodes.label: thm:SignTargetSet_card

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Direct enumeration: for $p, q > 0$ the set $\{(\pm p, \pm q)\}$ has $4$ elements, with corner cases $p = 0$ or $q = 0$ handled by dedupe.
nodes.statement_short: Direct enumeration with deduplication at zero.

nodes.name: Lemma 11.1(b) — abstract bijection
nodes.statement: Abstract form: given finite types $\alpha \simeq \beta$ of equal cardinality and an injection $f : \alpha \to \beta$, $f$ is a bijection.
nodes.statement_short: An injection between finite types of equal cardinality is a bijection.
assumptions: given finite types $\alpha \simeq \beta$ of equal cardinality and an injection $f : \alpha \to \beta$
nodes.label: lem:11_1_b_abstract

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: A finite type $\alpha$ with an injection into $\beta$ and an equivalence $\alpha \simeq \beta$ satisfies $|\alpha| = |\beta|$; an injective map between finite sets of equal cardinality is bijective.
nodes.statement_short: Injective map between finite sets of equal size is bijective.

nodes.name: Lemma 11.1(b) D-type bijection
nodes.statement: D-type specialisation: when $\mathbf{r}_1(\check{\mathcal{O}}) = 1$, the map $\PBP_D(\check{\mathcal{O}}) \times \mathrm{Fin}\,2 \to \MYD_D(\mathcal{O})$ given by $(\tau, \eps) \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\tau \otimes (\eps, \eps)$ is a bijection, with explicit $|\PBP_D(\ldots)| = 4m + 4$ card match.
nodes.statement_short: When r_1 = 1, (tau, eps) -> L_tau twisted is a bijection PBP_D x Fin 2 -> MYD_D.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:11_1_b_abstract} with $\alpha = \PBP_D(\check{\mathcal{O}}) \times \mathrm{Fin}\,2$ and $\beta = \MYD_D(\mathcal{O})$; the cardinality match follows from the explicit $4m + 4$ formula (Theorem~\ref{thm:SignTargetSet_card}).
nodes.statement_short: Apply the abstract bijection lemma with the explicit 4m+4 cardinality.

nodes.name: Prop 11.8 (AC level)
nodes.statement:
For $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-\}$ and tail symbol $x_	au$:  egin{enumerate} \item[(a)] $\mathcal{L}_	au 
eq 0$. \item[(b)] $x_	au = s \Rightarrow \mathcal{L}_	au^+ = 0$ and $\mathcal{L}_	au^- = 0$. \item[(c)] $x_	au \in \{r, c\} \Rightarrow \mathcal{L}_	au^+ 
eq 0$ and $\mathcal{L}_	au^- = 0$. \item[(d)] $x_	au = d \Rightarrow \mathcal{L}_	au^+ 
eq 0$ and $\mathcal{L}_	au^- 
eq 0$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Non-vanishing pattern of L_tau and its truncations according to the tail symbol x_tau.
assumptions: For $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-\}$ and tail symbol $x_\tau$:
nodes.label: prop:11_8_ac

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By case on $x_\tau$. From Lem~\ref{lem:11_6_D}: $\mathcal{E}(1) = (p_{\tau_t}, (-1)^{\eps_\tau} q_{\tau_t})$. \begin{itemize} \item $x_\tau = s$: by Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}, $p_{\tau_t} = 0$ and $\eps_\tau = 1$ (since $x_\tau \neq d$), $q_{\tau_t} \geq 2$. Truncations $\Lambda_{(1, 0)}$ and $\Lambda_{(0, 1)}$ both fail (containment checks). \item $x_\tau \in \{r, c\}$: $p_{\tau_t} \geq 1$, $\eps_\tau = 1$. $\Lambda_{(1, 0)}$ succeeds; $\Lambda_{(0, 1)}$ fails (since the second component is non-positive). \item $x_\tau = d$: $p_{\tau_t} \geq 1, q_{\tau_t} \geq 1, \eps_\tau = 0$. Both truncations succeed. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on x_tau using the first-entry formula and Prop 11.3; check the truncation containments.

nodes.name: Prop 11.9 D — numerical constraint on cross-twist
nodes.statement: Assume $\tau_1, \tau_2 \in \PBP_D$ with $h_{\mathrm{tail}}$ satisfied, $x_{\tau_1} = d$, and the cross-twist first-component equation $-p_{\tau_1, t} = p_{\tau_2, t} - 1$, plus $x_{\tau_2} \neq s$: \emph{contradiction}.
nodes.statement_short: Cross-twist numerical constraint with x_tau1 = d and x_tau2 != s is contradictory.
nodes.label: prop:11_9_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $x_{\tau_1} = d$ and $x_{\tau_1} \neq s$ $\Rightarrow p_{\tau_1, t} \geq 1$ (by Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}). So $-p_{\tau_1, t} \leq -1$. Then $p_{\tau_2, t} - 1 \leq -1$ $\Rightarrow p_{\tau_2, t} \leq 0$. With $p_{\tau_2, t} \geq 0$ (Lem~\ref{lem:tailSig_nonneg}), $p_{\tau_2, t} = 0$. By Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}, $p_{\tau_2, t} = 0 \iff x_{\tau_2} = s$, contradicting $x_{\tau_2} \neq s$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound p_t via Prop 11.3 and nonnegativity, forcing x_tau2 = s, a contradiction.
