nodes.name: Prop 11.10 — tail signatures equal from equal AC
nodes.statement: If $L_1 = L_2 \in \mathrm{ACResult}$ are non-empty with each branch having the same first entry formula as $\tau_1, \tau_2$, then $(p_{\tau_1, t}, q_{\tau_1, t}) = (p_{\tau_2, t}, q_{\tau_2, t})$.
nodes.statement_short: Equal non-empty AC results force equal tail signatures.
nodes.label: prop:11_10_D

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:11_6_D}, each branch of $L_i$ has first entry $(p_{\tau_i, t}, (-1)^{\eps} q_{\tau_i, t})$. If $L_1 = L_2$, their first entries coincide, so the $p_t$ and $\pm q_t$ coordinates match.
nodes.statement_short: Compare first entries using Lemma 11.6.

nodes.name: Prop 11.11 — no det twist
nodes.statement: There exist no $\tau_1, \tau_2$ with $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1) = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$ (the \emph{det twist} would require impossible sign configurations).
nodes.statement_short: No pair tau1, tau2 is related by the det twist of their associated cycles.
nodes.label: lem:11_11

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The $\otimes(1, 1)$ twist negates the first entry: $(\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1))^+ = 0$ always. So $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}^+ = 0$, forcing $x_{\tau_2} = s$ (Prop~\ref{prop:11_8_ac}(b)). But then $(\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1))^- \neq 0$ while $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}^- = 0$: contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: The twist kills L^+, forcing x_tau2 = s by Prop 11.8(b), then L^- gives a contradiction.

nodes.name: Prop 11.12 — injectivity modulo $\eps$
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (\eps_1, \eps_1) = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2} \otimes (\eps_2, \eps_2)$, then $\eps_1 = \eps_2$, $\eps_{\tau_1} = \eps_{\tau_2}$, and $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Twisted associated cycles that agree force equal twists, equal eps_tau and equal L_tau.
nodes.label: prop:11_12

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: If $\eps_1 \neq \eps_2$, the equation $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1) = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$ arises (via $\eps_1 \oplus \eps_2 = 1$), forbidden by Lem~\ref{lem:11_11}. So $\eps_1 = \eps_2$; cancellation gives $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$. Then $\eps_{\tau_1} = \eps_{\tau_2}$ follows from Prop~\ref{prop:11_8_ac}'s truncation pattern.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out eps1 != eps2 by Prop 11.11, cancel, and recover eps_tau from the truncation pattern.

nodes.name: Prop 11.13 — chain injectivity
nodes.statement: Full AC.fold chain injectivity: equal outputs $\Rightarrow$ equal chains $\Rightarrow$ equal input PBPs.
nodes.statement_short: AC.fold chain injectivity: equal outputs give equal input PBPs.
nodes.label: prop:11_13

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By Prop.~\ref{prop:11_12} we recover $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$ and matching $\eps$; the chain injectivity then descends to the inputs via invertibility of each AC.step.
nodes.statement_short: Recover L and eps by Prop 11.12, then invert each AC.step.

nodes.name: Prop 11.14 — surjectivity from counting
nodes.statement: Given a finite $\alpha$, a finite $\beta$, an injection $f : \alpha \to \beta$, and an equivalence $e : \alpha \simeq \beta$ witnessing $|\alpha| = |\beta|$: $f$ is surjective. Applied with $\alpha = \PBP_\gamma \times \mathrm{Fin}\,2$ and $\beta = \MYD_\gamma$, with injectivity from Prop~\ref{prop:11_12} and card match from Section~10 counting.
nodes.statement_short: An injection between finite sets of equal cardinality is surjective; applied to PBP x Fin 2 -> MYD.
assumptions: Given a finite $\alpha$, a finite $\beta$, an injection $f : \alpha \to \beta$, and an equivalence $e : \alpha \simeq \beta$ witnessing $|\alpha| = |\beta|$:
nodes.label: prop:11_14

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: A finite injective map into a finite set of equal cardinality is surjective; apply to $f : \alpha \to \beta$ with the cardinality witness $e : \alpha \simeq \beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Finite injective map into a set of equal size is surjective.

nodes.name: Prop 11.15 — main bijection for B/D types
nodes.statement: The map $(\tau, \eps) \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\tau \otimes (\eps, \eps)$ is a bijection \[ \PBP_\gamma(\check{\mathcal{O}}) \times \mathrm{Fin}\,2 \ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \MYD_\gamma(\mathcal{O}) \] for $\gamma \in \{D, B^+, B^-\}$.
nodes.statement_short: (tau, eps) -> L_tau twisted by (eps,eps) is a bijection PBP x Fin 2 -> MYD for D, B+, B-.
nodes.label: prop:11_15

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Injectivity follows from Prop.~\ref{prop:11_12} plus Prop.~\ref{prop:11_13}. Surjectivity follows from Prop.~\ref{prop:11_14} with card match from Prop.~\ref{prop:10_11_B}/\ref{prop:10_11_D}.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity from Props 11.12-11.13; surjectivity from Prop 11.14 with Section 10 counting.

nodes.name: Prop 11.16 — C/$\tilde{C}$ bijection from counting
nodes.statement: Paper Prop~11.16 (descent bijectivity for C/$\tilde{C}$ types) is captured at the PBP level by the Section~10 counting equalities (Prop.~\ref{prop:10_12_C}, \ref{prop:10_12_M}). The abstract wrapper presented here re-exposes the result via $\mathrm{surjectivity\_from\_counting}$: an injective map between finite sets of equal cardinality is bijective.
nodes.statement_short: C/C~ descent bijectivity, captured via the Section 10 counting equalities and surjectivity from counting.
nodes.label: prop:11_16

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Prop.~\ref{prop:11_14} with $\alpha = \PBP_C(\check{\mathcal{O}})$ and card match from Prop.~\ref{prop:10_12_C}; analogously for $\tilde{C}$ using Prop.~\ref{prop:10_12_M}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Prop 11.14 with the C and M counting formulas.

nodes.name: Prop 11.17 — main bijection for C/$\tilde{C}$
nodes.statement: For $\star \in \{C, \tilde{C}\}$: $\tau \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\tau$ is a bijection $\PBP_\star(\check{\mathcal{O}}) \xrightarrow{\sim} \MYD_\star(\mathcal{O})$.
nodes.statement_short: tau -> L_tau is a bijection PBP -> MYD for types C and C~.
nodes.label: prop:11_17

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Combine injectivity (from Prop.~\ref{prop:11_12}) with card match (Prop.~\ref{prop:10_12_C}/\ref{prop:10_12_M}) via Prop.~\ref{prop:11_14}.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity from Prop 11.12 plus counting via Prop 11.14.

nodes.name: Main bijection witness is not conditional
nodes.statement:
Main bijection (\ref{prop:11_14}, \ref{prop:11_15}, \ref{prop:11_17}) uses the
  abstract $\alpha \simeq \beta$ witness. Mathematically this is solid:
  an injective map from a finite type $\alpha$ into a finite type $\beta$ with
  an equivalence $e : \alpha \simeq \beta$ (i.e.\ $|\alpha| = |\beta|$) is
  automatically surjective. The witness $e$ is supplied from the Section~10
  counting formulas plus other enumeration data — this does not make the
  theorem conditional on any open assumption.
nodes.statement_short: The main bijection uses an abstract equivalence witness from counting; injective plus equal finite cardinality gives surjectivity.

nodes.name: (1) d sits at the bottom by monotonicity
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(1)} By layer monotonicity in column~0, a symbol $d$ (with maximal
  $\mathrm{layerOrd} = 4$) can only appear at the bottom.
  Conversely, $\eps_\tau = 0$ iff $d$ is present somewhere in column~0, which
  by monotonicity forces it to the bottom, i.e., $x_\tau = d$.

nodes.name: (2) p_t = 0 iff all tail cells are s
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(2)} $p_{\tau_t} = \sum_i \mathrm{tailContrib}(x_i).p$, and
  $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).p = 0$ only for $\sigma = s$. Combined with
  the non-negativity of each term, $p_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff $ every tail cell is $s$.

  Now the equivalence ``every tail cell is $s$'' $\iff$ $x_\tau = s$ follows
  from layer monotonicity: $x_\tau = s$ means the $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ at the
  bottom is $1$; all cells above have $\mathrm{layerOrd} \leq 1$; combined
  with non-dot (every tail cell is non-$\bullet$ by $\mathrm{dot\_match}$),
  every cell has $\mathrm{layerOrd} = 1$, i.e., equals $s$.
nodes.statement_short: (2) p_t = 0 iff all tail cells are s

nodes.name: p_t = 0 iff every tail cell is s via tailContrib

nodes.name: All-s iff x_tau = s by monotonicity and dot_match
nodes.statement:
Now the equivalence ``every tail cell is $s$'' $\iff$ $x_\tau = s$ follows
  from layer monotonicity: $x_\tau = s$ means the $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ at the
  bottom is $1$; all cells above have $\mathrm{layerOrd} \leq 1$; combined
  with non-dot (every tail cell is non-$\bullet$ by $\mathrm{dot\_match}$),
  every cell has $\mathrm{layerOrd} = 1$, i.e., equals $s$.
nodes.statement_short: All-s iff x_tau = s by monotonicity and dot_match

nodes.name: (3) q_t = 0 iff all tail cells are r iff x_1 = x_tau = r
nodes.statement:
\textbf{(3)} $q_{\tau_t} = \sum_i \mathrm{tailContrib}(x_i).q$, and
  $\mathrm{tailContrib}(\sigma).q = 0$ only for $\sigma = r$. So
  $q_{\tau_t} = 0 \iff$ every tail cell is $r$.

  The second equivalence: ``every tail cell is $r$'' $\iff$ $x_1 = r$ and
  $x_\tau = r$. Layer monotonicity gives
  $\mathrm{layerOrd}(x_1) \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_\tau)$
  for every tail cell $x_i$. If $x_1 = x_\tau = r$ (both equal $2$), then
  every $x_i$ has $\mathrm{layerOrd}$ sandwiched as $2 \leq \mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) \leq 2$,
  so $\mathrm{layerOrd}(x_i) = 2$, i.e., $x_i = r$. The converse is trivial.
nodes.statement_short: (3) q_t = 0 iff all tail cells are r iff x_1 = x_tau = r

nodes.name: Case on x_tau; first entry formula from Lemma 11.6
nodes.statement:
By case on $x_\tau$. From Lem~\ref{lem:11_6_D}:
  $\mathcal{E}(1) = (p_{\tau_t}, (-1)^{\eps_\tau} q_{\tau_t})$.
nodes.statement_short: Case on x_tau; first entry formula from Lemma 11.6

nodes.name: x = s: both truncations fail
nodes.statement: $x_\tau = s$: by Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}, $p_{\tau_t} = 0$ and $\eps_\tau = 1$ (since $x_\tau \neq d$), $q_{\tau_t} \geq 2$. Truncations $\Lambda_{(1, 0)}$ and $\Lambda_{(0, 1)}$ both fail (containment checks).
nodes.statement_short: x = s: both truncations fail

nodes.name: x in {r,c}: only Lambda_(1,0) succeeds
nodes.statement: $x_\tau \in \{r, c\}$: $p_{\tau_t} \geq 1$, $\eps_\tau = 1$. $\Lambda_{(1, 0)}$ succeeds; $\Lambda_{(0, 1)}$ fails (since the second component is non-positive).
nodes.statement_short: x in {r,c}: only Lambda_(1,0) succeeds

nodes.name: x = d: both truncations succeed
nodes.statement: $x_\tau = d$: $p_{\tau_t} \geq 1, q_{\tau_t} \geq 1, \eps_\tau = 0$. Both truncations succeed.
nodes.statement_short: x = d: both truncations succeed

nodes.name: x_tau1 = d gives p_{tau1,t} >= 1 by Prop 11.3
nodes.statement:
$x_{\tau_1} = d$ and $x_{\tau_1} \neq s$ $\Rightarrow p_{\tau_1, t} \geq 1$ (by Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}).
  So $-p_{\tau_1, t} \leq -1$.
nodes.statement_short: x_tau1 = d gives p_{tau1,t} >= 1 by Prop 11.3

nodes.name: Force p_{tau2,t} = 0 using nonnegativity
nodes.statement: Then $p_{\tau_2, t} - 1 \leq -1$ $\Rightarrow p_{\tau_2, t} \leq 0$. With $p_{\tau_2, t} \geq 0$ (Lem~\ref{lem:tailSig_nonneg}), $p_{\tau_2, t} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Force p_{tau2,t} = 0 using nonnegativity

nodes.name: Prop 11.3 gives x_tau2 = s, contradiction
nodes.statement: By Lem~\ref{lem:11_3}, $p_{\tau_2, t} = 0 \iff x_{\tau_2} = s$, contradicting $x_{\tau_2} \neq s$.
nodes.statement_short: Prop 11.3 gives x_tau2 = s, contradiction

nodes.name: Det twist kills the + part
nodes.statement: The $\otimes(1, 1)$ twist negates the first entry: $(\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1))^+ = 0$ always.
nodes.statement_short: Det twist kills the + part

nodes.name: Prop 11.8(b) forces x_tau2 = s
nodes.statement: So $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}^+ = 0$, forcing $x_{\tau_2} = s$ (Prop~\ref{prop:11_8_ac}(b)).
nodes.statement_short: Prop 11.8(b) forces x_tau2 = s

nodes.name: Minus parts disagree: contradiction
nodes.statement: But then $(\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1))^- \neq 0$ while $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}^- = 0$: contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Minus parts disagree: contradiction

nodes.name: eps1 != eps2 contradicts Prop 11.11
nodes.statement: If $\eps_1 \neq \eps_2$, the equation $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} \otimes (1, 1) = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$ arises (via $\eps_1 \oplus \eps_2 = 1$), forbidden by Lem~\ref{lem:11_11}.
nodes.statement_short: eps1 != eps2 contradicts Prop 11.11

nodes.name: Cancel the twist
nodes.statement: So $\eps_1 = \eps_2$; cancellation gives $\mathcal{L}_{\tau_1} = \mathcal{L}_{\tau_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cancel the twist

nodes.name: Recover eps_tau from Prop 11.8
nodes.statement: Then $\eps_{\tau_1} = \eps_{\tau_2}$ follows from Prop~\ref{prop:11_8_ac}'s truncation pattern.
nodes.statement_short: Recover eps_tau from Prop 11.8
